name: CKM
summary: CKM, the muscle form of creatine kinase, on chromosome 10: an enzyme that regenerates ATP in muscle during very short, very hard effort. One variant, g.15884567G>A in intron 4 (EquCab2.0; BIEC2-109575), was reported by Gu et al. in 2010: the A allele was commoner among elite Thoroughbred racehorses than among horses that had never won. The result did not hold up in that study's own independent sample of 130 horses, a later Quarter Horse study found no link with racing performance, and an Italian Trotter study of 2021 (412 horses) found none with harness-racing traits. That study's marker, g.16079732G>A on EquCab3.0, is taken to be the same SNP on the newer assembly - same gene, same change, and the authors treat it as Gu et al.'s marker - but no source states the conversion. A horse of about 16,000 years ago already carried the A allele, so it is old standing variation; that G, the reference allele, came first is inferred, not shown. It is a candidate that failed to replicate: no effect of either allele on speed, distance, stamina or anything else is established. NCBI and the original marker description both place it on chromosome 10. T here is the A of the papers, the allele proposed as favourable, and C is their G.
